newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Nov 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - London Evening Standard - Nov 7.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company

Today in Tasmania, the gunman that massacred 35 people in the world's worst mass murder in April this year admitted to the killings in court. Martin Bryant laughed at survivors of the tragedy so hard that he could barely say the word "guilty.'
COLT ON LINE FOR A 350 MILLION STG FLOAT

Three year old telecommunications company Colt, owned by Fidelity Investments of the U.S., is expected to announce its flotation on London and New York stock markets as early as next week. The company could be valued at up to 350 million stg.
DOLLAR IN SPIN OVER JAPANESE PROP FEARS

Comments Japanese Ministry of Finance official Eisuke Sakakibara sent the dollar sliding on overnight trading. He said the dollar had recovered enough from last year's plunge against the yen and that his ministry would stop supporting the rise of the dollar.
BLOW FOR HOLLINGER OVER FAIRFAX STAKE

Australian Treasury and Communications ministers have rebuffed Hollinger International's attempts to double its stake in Fairfax Newspapers to 50 percent. Foreign ownership rules limit Conrad Black's Hollinger to a 25 percent stake.
There is now renewed speculation that Hollinger will be forced to sell.
FLEMING SHUTS DOOR ON ACTION GROUP'S CLAIMS

Robert Fleming the investment bank headed by John Manser has stated that it intends to oppose any future compensation claims against its Far Eastern joint venture Jardine Fleming, from an action group whose members lost money in the scandal involving fund manager Colin Armstrong. 12.4 million stg had already been offered to investors and it did not believe any further payments could be justified.
